newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends high on c.bank inaction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends high on c.bank inaction.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate rose to another 21-month high at close on Wednesday amid market disappointment over the central bank's failure to inject more funds into the market to loosen liquidity, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate eased at midday but resumed an uptrend in the afternoon as the central bank's inaction became apparent.

It closed at 8.558 percent against Tuesday's 8.395 finish -- far outside the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent and marking the rate's highest level since it hit 8.774 percent on September 15, 1995.
Tuesday's finish also was a 21-month peak.

The 30-day commercial paper stabilised at 8.00-8.50 percent against 8.00-8.75 after the central bank on Tuesday injected T$20 billion into the funds-strapped market through a novel "closed" operation -- letting a state-run bank withdraw that amount of its redeposits to replenish liquidity.
The money rates have been skyrocketing on a torrent of funds flowing out of the banking system into a red-hot bourse that has gained more than 300 points or three percent since June 16.
The overnight rate stood at 5.977 percent on June 16.
Dealers said the rates' movements on Thursday would depend mainly on whether the central bank acts to inject more funds.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.8700 percent against 5.8600.
